senses.definition: To make a quick push or tap with a finger or narrow object.
senses.example: I poked a small hole in the clay with a twig.

senses.definition: To stick out from or push through something.
senses.example: The first green leaves poked through the soil.

senses.definition: To rub a surface so that it becomes smooth or shiny.
senses.example: We polished the old doorknob until it gleamed.

senses.definition: A substance used to make a surface shine or to add a smooth coating.
senses.example: The floor had a fresh coat of polish.

senses.definition: To improve the small details of a piece of work.
senses.example: I polished my story by changing the ending.

senses.definition: Showing respect and care for other people in how you speak or act.
senses.example: It was polite to wait until she finished speaking.

senses.definition: The tiny grains that seed plants make and move by wind, animals, or other means. The grains carry cells that help the plant make seeds.
senses.example: Yellow pollen stuck to the bumblebee’s legs.

senses.definition: The moving of pollen to a part of a plant that can receive it, a step that can help the plant make seeds.
senses.example: Bees help with pollination when they carry pollen from flower to flower.

senses.definition: An animal that carries pollen so it can reach the part of a plant that receives it.
senses.example: A butterfly can be a pollinator when it visits a flower for food.

senses.definition: A closed flat shape made by joining straight sides.
senses.example: A rectangle and a triangle are both polygons.

senses.definition: A material made of very long molecules built from many smaller pieces joined in chains or networks.
senses.example: Cellulose, which helps plants stay strong, is a natural polymer.

senses.definition: A fairly small area of water surrounded by land.
senses.example: A frog jumped into the pond when we came near.

senses.definition: Liked or chosen by many people.
senses.example: The swings are popular at our playground.

senses.definition: Light or small enough to carry and use in different places.
senses.example: We brought a portable speaker to the picnic.

senses.definition: A picture made to show a person, often their face.
senses.example: I painted a portrait of my sister sitting near the window.

senses.definition: The place where something or someone is, or the way they are arranged.
senses.example: The stool was in a good position for reaching the bottom shelf.

senses.definition: A job or role, especially one with certain duties.
senses.example: My position on the soccer team is goalkeeper.

senses.definition: To put something where you want it to be.
senses.example: We positioned the lamp beside the drawing table.

senses.definition: Able to happen or be done.
senses.example: It is possible to make a kite with only paper, sticks, and string.

senses.definition: A large printed sign or picture put up for people to see.
senses.example: We hung a poster for the bake sale outside the gym.

senses.definition: Things made from clay that has been shaped and hardened with heat.
senses.example: The museum displayed pottery with birds painted on it.

senses.definition: To make a liquid or many small pieces flow out of a container.
senses.example: I poured the beans from the bag into the bowl.

senses.definition: To come down or move in a heavy flow.
senses.example: Rain poured off the roof all afternoon.

senses.definition: A dry substance made up of very fine bits.
senses.example: The white powder in the bag was flour.

senses.definition: Able to do something with a lot of strength, energy, or influence.
senses.example: A powerful motor lifts the gate.

senses.definition: Useful or sensible for a real job or situation.
senses.example: A bag with two straps is practical for carrying heavy books.

senses.definition: Time spent doing something again and again to get better at it.
senses.example: After a week of practice I could play the tune.

senses.definition: To do something many times so you can improve at it.
senses.example: I practice my spelling words for ten minutes after school.

senses.definition: A broad area of grassland, often with very few trees. The name is used especially for grasslands in central North America.
senses.example: In summer, wildflowers dotted the tall grass of the prairie.

senses.definition: To say that you admire or approve of someone or something.
senses.example: We praised our teammate for helping the new player.

senses.definition: Words or actions that show that you approve of someone’s work or behavior.
senses.example: The class received praise for cleaning up the yard.

senses.definition: Before, or earlier than.
senses.example: To preview a movie is to see some or all of it before most people can.

senses.definition: Of great value, whether because it costs a lot or matters a lot to someone.
senses.example: The little note from Grandma is precious to me.

senses.definition: Water that falls from clouds as rain, snow, sleet, or hail.
senses.example: Our weather chart shows how much precipitation fell overnight.

senses.definition: An animal that catches and eats other animals.
senses.example: The cheetah is a predator that can run fast for a short time.

senses.definition: To say what you think will happen, often based on patterns or other clues.
senses.example: I predict that the ice cube near the window will melt first.

senses.definition: To like or want one thing more than another.
senses.example: I prefer to play outside when the sun is shining.

senses.definition: Better or more suitable than another choice.
senses.example: The shady path was preferable on a hot afternoon.

senses.definition: A word part added at the beginning of another word or word part that helps change its meaning.
senses.example: The prefix re- in rebuild shows that the building happens again.

senses.definition: To make something ready for use or get ready to do something.
senses.example: We prepared the art table with paper, water, and brushes.

entries.pronunciation: noun and adjective: PREZ-unt, verb: prih-ZENT

senses.definition: A gift someone gives to another person.
senses.example: Sofia wrapped a small present for her cousin.

senses.definition: Here or taking part now.
senses.example: All the players were present when practice began.

senses.definition: Happening or existing now.
senses.example: The present schedule has two more games on it.

senses.definition: To give, show, or explain something to other people.
senses.example: I will present my poster to the class tomorrow.

senses.definition: A pot that traps steam under a tight lid so food can cook at a higher temperature.
senses.example: The pressure cooker trapped steam while dinner cooked.

senses.definition: Kept at a set air or fluid pressure, often higher than the pressure outside.
senses.example: The inside of a space suit is pressurized so the astronaut’s body can function.

senses.definition: To act as if something is true for fun or to make someone believe it.
senses.example: We pretended the pile of cushions was a castle.

senses.definition: A baked bread snack, often twisted into a shape with loops and sprinkled with salt.
senses.example: I saved a pretzel to eat after the hike.

senses.definition: The amount you must pay to buy something.
senses.example: The price of each postcard was one dollar.

senses.definition: To decide how much someone must pay for something.
senses.example: We priced each cookie at fifty cents for the sale.

senses.definition: A living thing that makes its own food and provides a first source of food for other things in a food chain.
senses.example: The grass in a meadow is a primary producer that can feed grasshoppers and rabbits.

senses.definition: A way to write a whole number greater than one as prime numbers multiplied together.
senses.example: The prime factorization of 18 is two times three times three.

senses.definition: A whole number greater than one with exactly two positive factors, one and itself.
senses.example: Seven is a prime number since only one and seven divide it evenly.

senses.definition: To make words or pictures appear on paper using ink, a printer, or another method.
senses.example: We printed the map before leaving the house.

senses.definition: To write letters separately rather than joining them.
senses.example: Please print your first name on the label.

senses.definition: A mark left by pressure or a copy of a picture made by printing.
senses.example: The old floorboard held the dusty print of a paw.

senses.definition: Making art by transferring a design from a surface, like a block or plate, to paper, cloth, or another surface.
senses.example: In printmaking class we pressed our inked blocks onto paper to make several copies.

senses.definition: The ability to choose which parts of your life or information other people can see.
senses.example: I asked an adult to help change the game’s privacy setting.

senses.definition: Belonging to one person or group, or meant to be kept from others.
senses.example: The notebook was private, so I asked before reading it.

senses.definition: Something given to a person who wins or does something especially well.
senses.example: Our team won a book as a prize.

senses.definition: To value something a great deal.
senses.example: I prize the smooth stone my cousin gave me.

senses.definition: A number telling how likely an event is to happen.
senses.example: The probability of heads on a fair coin is one half.

senses.definition: Something difficult that needs to be fixed, answered, or worked out.
senses.example: The broken latch was a problem because the gate would not stay shut.

senses.definition: A question that gives you information to work with and asks you to find an answer.
senses.example: The last math problem asked how many tiles would cover the floor.

senses.definition: A chip or group of parts that follows instructions to do the work of a computer.
senses.example: The processor can quickly work out how to move the shapes on the screen.

senses.definition: An official statement meant to be heard or read by the public.
senses.example: The president issued a proclamation to announce the decision.

senses.definition: To make, grow, or bring about something.
senses.example: The apple tree produced more fruit this year.

senses.definition: Fresh food grown as crops, especially vegetables and fruit.
senses.example: We chose tomatoes from the produce stand.

senses.definition: A group of instructions a computer can follow.
senses.example: A program adds up how many points I earned.

senses.definition: Movement toward finishing something or getting better at it.
senses.example: The first two rows of tiles showed good progress.

senses.definition: To move toward a later or better stage.
senses.example: The repairs progressed after the missing parts arrived.

senses.definition: A way to show the curved surface of Earth on a flat map. Each way changes some distances, shapes, or sizes.
senses.example: The map’s projection made Greenland look bigger compared with Africa than it really is.

senses.definition: An image that light sends onto a screen, wall, or other surface.
senses.example: We watched the projection of the photos on the classroom wall.

senses.definition: Words that say what you will certainly do or what will happen.
senses.example: Jules kept her promise to return the book on Friday.

senses.definition: To say that you are sure you will do something or that it will happen.
senses.example: I promised to save my sister a seat.

senses.definition: Right or suitable for the situation, or following a rule or accepted practice.
senses.example: It is proper to return a borrowed book in good condition.

senses.definition: To keep someone or something safe from harm or damage.
senses.example: The case protects my glasses when I put them in my bag.

senses.definition: A material built from small parts called amino acids. Different proteins have different jobs in living things.
senses.example: One protein in my blood carries oxygen.

senses.definition: An action or event that shows people strongly disagree with something.
senses.example: The families held a protest asking the town to keep the park open.

senses.definition: To say or show that you strongly disagree with something.
senses.example: I protested when the game ended before our final turn.

senses.definition: Pleased because you or someone you care about did something well.
senses.example: I was proud of my friend when she finished the steep climb.

senses.definition: A large area within a country that has a name and its own local government in many places.
senses.example: Ontario is a province in Canada.

senses.definition: Work or help provided for people by a government or another group acting for it.
senses.example: Fire protection is a public service our town helps pay for.

senses.definition: To make writing, pictures, or other work available for people to read or see.
senses.example: Our class plans to publish a book of poems.

senses.definition: A small flat disk moved with sticks in ice hockey.
senses.example: The puck slid across the ice to the other player.

senses.definition: A small shallow pool of water or another liquid on a surface.
senses.example: I stepped over a puddle at the corner.

senses.definition: A quick small burst of air, smoke, or steam.
senses.example: A puff of air from the window moved the paper.

senses.definition: To send out air or smoke in small bursts.
senses.example: The old train puffed steam as it started up.

senses.definition: To move something toward you or in the direction you are moving.
senses.example: Pull the wagon toward the shed.

senses.definition: A steady or sudden force that draws something closer.
senses.example: One pull on the curtain cord opened the curtains.

senses.definition: A wheel with a groove along its edge that guides a rope or cable.
senses.example: The rope passed over a pulley so we could pull down to lift the flag.

senses.definition: A wet mixture of little fibers used to make paper.
senses.example: The paper machine squeezed water out of the pulp.

senses.definition: A beat you can feel when pressure from the heart moves through an artery.
senses.example: A heartbeat starts the pressure change you notice as a pulse.

senses.definition: Arriving or happening at the time that was planned.
senses.example: Lena was punctual and got to the bus stop before we left.

senses.definition: A small hole made by something sharp.
senses.example: A puncture in the tire let the air out.

senses.definition: To make a hole by poking or piercing something.
senses.example: A sharp thorn punctured the soft rubber.

senses.definition: A penalty received after breaking a rule or doing something wrong.
senses.example: The referee gave the team a time penalty as punishment for breaking the rule.

senses.definition: The round opening that lets light into an eye.
senses.example: My pupil becomes smaller in bright light.

senses.definition: A figure moved by someone’s hands, strings, or rods, often to act out a story.
senses.example: We made a puppet from a sock and two paper eyes.

senses.definition: To buy something.
senses.example: We purchased two tickets before getting on the ferry.

senses.definition: Something you buy, or the act of buying it.
senses.example: The bird guide was my favorite purchase at the sale.

senses.definition: Made of just one thing with nothing else mixed in.
senses.example: The shop sold pure apple juice with no added sweetener.

senses.definition: The reason for doing something or the job a thing was made to do.
senses.example: The purpose of the covering is to keep rain off the seats.

senses.definition: To use force to move something away from you or in a certain direction.
senses.example: We pushed the cart toward the old gate.

senses.definition: A movement or force that presses something in a direction.
senses.example: One strong push sent the empty sled down the hill.

senses.definition: To move or place someone or something somewhere.
senses.example: I put the dirty cup beside the sink.

senses.definition: To express an idea in a certain way.
senses.example: “Let’s give it another try” is a kind way to put it.

senses.definition: To return something to a storage place after using it.
senses.example: We put away the paintbrushes after washing them.

senses.definition: To move something you planned to do to a later time.
senses.example: Rain forced us to put off the picnic for a day.

senses.definition: To notice how separate clues fit and use them to work out what probably happened.
senses.example: When I saw muddy boots and tracks by the door, I put two and two together.
